citation.title: Body, Mind, or Heart? Investigating the Sufficient and Necessary Factors for Robot Acceptance Among Middle-Aged and Older Chinese Adults

reading.source_scope_note: Cross-sectional online survey of407 community-dwelling Hangzhou adults aged51–79 after a silent two-minute NAO video. Respondents rate13 capacity items,negative attitudes,trust and stated future use/recommendation. Set-ESEM and NCA analyze associations and sample ceiling constraints; no randomized mind manipulation,actual adoption,longitudinal outcome or causal necessity/sufficiency is established.
access_limits: All supplied text,items,tables and figure read. Data available only on reasonable request to the author; no contact made and no participant data,model output or executable analyses obtained. No public supporting-information packet identified.
The edited silent NAO stimulus is described and a YouTube reference supplied; the actual edited stimulus was not obtained or watched. Appearance and context are not experimentally compared.

NCA empirical bounds,scatterplots,ceiling diagnostics and exact percentage conversion are unavailable. Printed bottleneck values are retained without manufacturing a universal threshold or guessing raw-score replacements.

Original mind-perception,trust,NARS,NCA and theory-source articles/books are not independently fully read. Crossref identity checks and metadata-only confirmation do not add independent original-paper credit.
The clinical/care literature cited in the introduction is secondary. This survey is not evidence of dementia treatment benefit,medical safety or suitability for an individual care decision.

study.sample: 465 responses minus54 failing attention criteria gives411; four further quality exclusions gives407. Checks include robot identification,instructed response and diligence,plus time,longstring/variability,consistency and multivariate outliers. No missing data reported. Ages51–79,mean56.16,SD4.56;234men,173women;44%prior robot experience. Urban community recruitment with online survey limits generality to frailer,older,rural or digitally excluded groups.
study.exposure: A two-minute silent,logo-removed NAO video precedes ratings. A single depicted robot and broad home-robot introduction cannot isolate robot type,appearance,sound,role or actual interaction effects.
study.measures: Body4 and mind4 and heart5 capacity judgments coded0/.5/1. Body includes sickness,pain,tiredness,fear; mind includes arithmetic,hearing,memory,distance sensing; heart includes pride,guilt,love,happiness,anger. Trust has three reliability/dependability items. NARS has13 items across three subscales,including three reverse-coded emotion items. Intention includes two near-duplicate six-month use statements and a recommendation item,not observed adoption.
study.models: MLR/geomin set-ESEM permits cross-loadings within the three mind factors and within three attitude factors,not across sets. NCA uses CR-FDH with10000 permutations. Prespecified sets and ordinal ratings treated through this estimator are modeling choices,not proof of universal three-factor architecture.
study.associations: Body positively relates to negative interaction attitudesβ.316,p.024,opposite the predicted sign; mind negatively relatesβ−.452,p<.001; heart negatively relates to negative emotion attitudesβ−.567,p<.001. Negative interaction/emotion attitudes relate to trust; trustβ.320,p.001 and emotion attitudesβ−.235,p.009 relate to intention. Several paths are null and separate significance does not test their differences. Reported R² is.542 for trust,.242 for intention.
study.necessity: NCA reports trust→intentiond.18,Table6p.001. No tested mind/attitude factor is significant as a necessary condition under the selected analysis. This is a sample-relative ceiling pattern,not proof that trust is causally irreplaceable in all populations or that a nonsignificant factor is unnecessary everywhere. A positive SEM coefficient is not formal logical or causal sufficiency.
study.validity: Table3 HTMT.959 for interaction/social influence contradicts all<.85. Correlation.706 exceeds the interaction diagonal.701,so the stated Fornell–Larcker success is not universal. AVEs.490/.470 for interaction/emotion are below.50. Common-method diagnostics and a null method-factor comparison do not establish absence of common-source bias.
study.interpretation: The study measures attributed capacities rather than actual cognition or feelings. Perceived fear/pain,body appearance,physiological sensors,privacy intrusion and uncanny-valley shape are not interchangeable. Calibrated reliance,not maximal trust or mere adoption,is the appropriate distinct evaluation target.

summary: No new entry. Enrich mind/experience attribution,performance trust and AI adoption intention with a bounded older-adult survey. Preserve opposing body/mind associations,null paths,three-factor modeling choices and absence of actual adoption evidence. Correct model-label and validity claims,retain unresolved fit/scaling discrepancies,and avoid turning NCA percentages or SEM associations into universal causal requirements.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a specific cross-sectional acceptance study and measurement limits rather than duplicate a capacity facet or instrument.
findings.evidence_scope: A407-person survey models attributed NAO body,mind and heart capacities using13 selected items and three prespecified sets. Body and mind have opposing associations with negative interaction attitudes; heart relates to emotion attitudes. No capacity dimension is significant as an NCA necessary condition under this analysis.
findings.boundary: This is one cross-sectional video context,not a randomized capacity effect or a universal three-factor architecture. Nonsignificant NCA does not prove nonnecessity everywhere. Actual robot capacities and human dignity are separate questions.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a specific cross-sectional acceptance study and measurement limits rather than duplicate a capacity facet or instrument.

evidence.quote: Does the NAO robot feel pain

findings.evidence_scope: The study separates body sensation/fear items from heart pride/guilt/love/happiness/anger items. Their attitudes associations differ within a chosen measurement model. This refines an existing broad experience umbrella rather than introducing every scale facet as a behavior.
findings.boundary: Body and heart are selected attribution facets,not verified feelings. Body sensation ratings are not physical appearance or privacy sensors. Positive and null paths do not establish an uncanny valley or a causal emotional mechanism.

findings.definition: Expecting an agent or system to perform competently and reliably in a relevant task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a specific cross-sectional acceptance study and measurement limits rather than duplicate a capacity facet or instrument.
findings.evidence_scope: Three trust,reliability and dependability ratings positively associate with intention. NCA reports a medium sample ceiling effectd.18,p.001 for trust and intention,without raw-data replication or a universal raw-score threshold.
findings.boundary: Perceived reliability is not actual safety or calibrated reliance. A path coefficient is not logical sufficiency,and sample necessity is not an intervention effect. Increasing trust without warranted capability can be harmful.

findings.definition: Plans or stated likelihood of incorporating AI technology into future activities.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a specific cross-sectional acceptance study and measurement limits rather than duplicate a capacity facet or instrument.

evidence.quote: would recommend others to use the robot

findings.evidence_scope: Future use/planning and recommendation statements form a three-item intention index after a video. Trust and emotion attitudes predict this index;reported explained variance.242. No later use,care outcome,purchase or authorized deployment is measured.
findings.boundary: Recommendation and personal adoption are related but distinct,and two use items are near duplicates. Intention,actual use,consent,competence and patient benefit differ. No one must adopt a robot or display greater trust.

findings.definition: Using assistance to a degree justified by its task-specific competence, relevance, uncertainty and the consequences of error.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a specific cross-sectional acceptance study and measurement limits rather than duplicate a capacity facet or instrument.

evidence.quote: prioritize strategies that directly build trust

findings.evidence_scope: The discussion proposes reliability,predictability,safety and transparency as trust-building supports,but evaluates no intervention or objective reliance calibration. These are recommendations,not demonstrated mechanisms here.
findings.boundary: Boundary only:high intention/trust is not necessarily appropriate reliance. Preserve informed refusal,real capability and oversight. No independent calibration-performance paper credit.

findings.definition: A drop in comfort or affinity when an artificial agent appears highly, but imperfectly, human-like, rather than a steady increase as human likeness rises.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a specific cross-sectional acceptance study and measurement limits rather than duplicate a capacity facet or instrument.

evidence.quote: valley eﬀect may be driven in part

findings.evidence_scope: The paper interprets body-attribution associations using an uncanny-valley account,but measures no graded human-likeness curve and does not manipulate bodily cues.
findings.boundary: A positive body-attitude association is not a local valley,actual discomfort mechanism or proof of privacy intrusion. Boundary note only;no independent measured uncanny-valley effect credit.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Text equates60%intention with4.2 and21.4%trust with1.5 on a1–7scale. If percentages refer to the full theoretical range,the origin-aware conversions are4.6 and2.284. NCA may instead use empirical scope,bounds unreported;retain Table7 percentages and do not substitute new raw thresholds without output.

Set-ESEM chi-square/df.602 is paired with positiveRMSEA.031. Conventional uncorrected RMSEA would be zero when chi-square<df,but MLR robust/scaled fit measures may differ. Exact estimator output is needed;do not silently replace a ratio or RMSEA.

Table4 raw chi-square difference175.152 anddfdifference40 differ from prose142.915/43. Robust scaled testing can change the test statistic,but not explain a different nested-model df difference by itself. Need exact compared models/output rather than a guessed correction.

Tolerance.426–.651 implies reciprocal VIFapproximately1.536–2.347 if referring to the same predictors,versus printed1.230–2.347. Different assessment sets or transcription may explain;unverified without output.

AVEs.490 and.470 are below.50;no inferential test supports wording not significantly lower. Printed primary loadings do not alone reconstruct every ESEM variance statistic when cross-loadings are omitted. Retain concerns without inventing a corrected reliability matrix.
Abstractp<.001 for d.18 versus Table6p.001. Precision/rounding may explain;use the table value with scope and do not invent the exact permutation result.

methodological_limits: Cross-sectional self-report from one urban,relatively young older-adult sample cannot establish direction,causal necessity/sufficiency or broad care-population generality.
One silent NAO video,selected capacity items,ordinal coding and modeling choices constrain inference. Three constructs are not universally established from one fitted model.
Validity claims have published-table exceptions. Common-method diagnostics and null fit comparisons do not establish absent method bias. Exact raw data/model output are unavailable.
NCA thresholds depend on scope,measurement,ceiling method and sample. A significant sample ceiling pattern is not a universal causal prerequisite;SEM associations are not logical sufficiency.

Intention/recommendation differ from actual adoption and clinical benefit. Building warranted trust requires capability,evidence and oversight,rather than appearance-based persuasion or removing informed refusal.
Cognitive/emotional attributions are not actual robot feelings or privacy mechanisms. Source repairs do not imply fabricated data or author misconduct.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Aggregate PCA and individual-level set-ESEM differ in unit,item selection and constraints. Preserve dimensional disagreement without declaring one universal structure.
The adoption-intention distinction persists:questionnaire plans are not observed behavior,competence or future benefit. Reliability/validity need explicit evidence rather than favorable scale labels.
Predetermined dimensions and translated/selected words require measurement scope. Body/mind/heart capacity ratings do not automatically measure state inference or actual capacities.
